version.changelog: Remove incomplete install metadata for Playwright setup

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and resource requirements are consistent with an automated Shanghai Library seat-booking tool; it requests no unrelated credentials and its browser automation / network activity align with the stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the implementation: Node.js scripts, Playwright-based browser-assisted login, and direct calls to the library API (yuyue.library.sh.cn). Required binaries (node, npm, npx) and Playwright are appropriate for the described functionality and nothing else (no unrelated cloud credentials or services are requested).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct the agent/user to run npm install and npx playwright install, to run login.js for interactive browser login, and to read/write profile auth JSON files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking (or a path you pass). Reading/writing those profile files and probing the library endpoints is necessary for the skill. There is no code that reads arbitrary system-wide credentials or transmits data to endpoints other than the documented library API. Note: login requires interactive manual login in a browser window (the script captures tokens afterward).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This registry entry contains code but no packaged install spec; SKILL.md instructs running npm install and npx playwright install. Those commands will fetch Playwright from the npm registry and download Chromium binaries from Playwright's hosting — expected for browser automation but a network download of large binaries will occur. No third-party/personal URLs or archive extracts are used in the repo itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or external credentials. It uses local profile files (~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json) to store accessToken/sign/timestamp and will generate x-encode locally. This is proportionate to its purpose; the skill does not request unrelated secrets or system-wide credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request permanent/global privileges. It writes/reads its own profile files in the user's config directory and does not modify other skills or global agent settings. Autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation: false) is the platform default and not an additional red flag here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be what it claims: a Node.js CLI that automates Shanghai Library seat booking using Playwright and direct API calls. Before installing: (1) Review and trust the repository source — the scripts will run npm install and download Playwright/Chromium binaries. (2) Understand the tool stores authentication tokens locally under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json — keep those files protected (chmod 600) and do not commit or share them. (3) The login flow opens a browser for you to manually sign in; run this on a machine where you can interact with the browser. (4) If you want to be extra cautious, run npm install in an isolated environment (container or VM) and inspect login.js/login_and_get_auth_node.js before use. Overall the requested permissions and network activity are consistent with booking seats and no unrelated credential exfiltration or external endpoints were observed.
